blocks.body:
## Technical summary

**Stop before the causal outcome.** Doubling the frozen sample to 30 participant-distinct videos produced complete, schema-valid outputs from both local visual paths, but it did not satisfy the unchanged triangulation gates. Gemma abstained on lag for an outward-rounded 80–90% of windows, above the frozen 50% maximum, and the conservative null/irrelevant envelope remained K=5-suppressed. No causal endpoint opened, so this is a failed calibration gate—not a causal null and not evidence about whether synchronized embodied cues help.

## The added sample did not rescue the two-model calibration

Both paths achieved 100% schema validity and full visual item coverage, which rules out malformed output as the explanation. The decisive problem is scientific usability: Qwen3-VL stayed below the lag-abstention ceiling, while Gemma did not. The figure shows the outward-rounded upper bounds against the prespecified ceiling.

## The endpoint remained closed by construction

The null/irrelevant range was still too sparse to export under K=5, even after the one permitted expansion. Because either failed gate is sufficient to stop, none of the synchronized-minus-absent, shuffled, shifted, or corrupted causal contrasts was run.

## Scope and metric definitions

The calibration covers exactly 30 participant-distinct items, 1,800 speech seconds, and 272 candidate windows from the authorized frozen ChildLens pilot. Rates are outward-rounded; small cells are suppressed at K=5. Local-model outputs are provisional measurement hypotheses, not German human labels or ground truth. Simulator-oracle labels would have been the only evaluation truth had the causal run opened.

## Method and validation record

The original 15 items and successful Qwen outputs were reused read-only. Fifteen additional participant-distinct items were selected content-blind, transferred sequentially, clipped locally, and processed offline. Qwen3-ASR, Qwen3-VL, and Gemma 4 E4B ran as separate instruments; model-specific estimates, disagreement, and abstention were preserved rather than majority-voted. The final extension suite passed 20 tests, and no restricted payload left quarantine.

## Limitations and claim boundary

There is no qualified German human gold, so model disagreement cannot be interpreted as reliability. The 30-item expansion was a disclosed post-failure attempt and cannot be expanded again under the frozen design. This report makes no ChildLens language-acquisition claim, no infant or BabyView generalization, and no statement about the synchronized-cue mechanism because the causal outcome was never run.

## Recommendation

**Do not present this as the intended Michael Frank mechanism nudge, and stop investing in the ChildLens pseudo-calibration branch.** If a near-term directional demo remains valuable, the clean next choice is a separately authorized synthetic-only simulator-oracle prototype with no ChildLens calibration claim. Otherwise, wait for a completely fresh BabyView-only study. The removed fallback is not activated here; either branch requires a new substantive user decision.

## Further questions

Would a transparent synthetic-only mechanism demonstration still be useful enough to justify one small one-shot run, or is the absence of a defensible naturalistic calibration anchor a reason to pause until BabyView access exists?
